short: Two years of campaigning erased Central Asia's richest empire and opened the west to the Mongols.
full:
In 1218 a Mongol trade caravan of some 450 men was seized at Otrar on the Syr Darya by its governor, Inalchuq, who accused them of spying and had them killed. Genghis Khan sent three envoys to demand redress; Shah Muhammad II beheaded one and shaved the beards of the others. The Mongol armies crossed the Tian Shan the following year.

The Khwarazmian empire stretched from the Aral Sea to the Persian Gulf and could field far more men than the invaders, but the Shah dispersed his forces among his cities. They were taken one at a time: Otrar, Bukhara, Samarkand, Urgench, Merv, Nishapur. Genghis appeared before Bukhara after crossing the Kyzylkum desert, a direction from which no army was expected. Muhammad fled west and died on an island in the Caspian in 1220. His son Jalal al-Din fought on until 1231. Contemporary estimates of the slaughter are unreliable but the region's irrigation and urban life took centuries to recover.
